Our team— Anish Kamatam , Ashwin Prabou , Mukesh Saravanan , and myself—built a powerful solution to tackle this problem head-on. We developed a GraphRAG system using Neo4j that maps comprehensive relationships between brand-name drugs and their generic equivalents. Our database includes active ingredients, potential interactions, and critical consumption warnings (like avoiding grapefruit juice with certain medications). We used a computer vision model(gemini) to read prescription handwriting, making the entire process frictionless for users. This project represents more than just a technical achievement—it's about making healthcare more accessible and transparent for everyone. Have you or someone you know ever been surprised by the cost of a prescription? 𝑾𝒆'𝒓𝒆 𝑪𝒂𝒍 𝑯𝒂𝒄𝒌𝒔 𝑾𝒊𝒏𝒏𝒆𝒓𝒔! 🎉 This Monday started like any other until a notification in my email caught me off guard: 𝐂𝐚𝐥 𝐇𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐳𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. A quick glance, and my curiosity was piqued. Could it be? I checked Devpost with my teammates— Adithya Gundlapalli , Abby Kaur , and Rushaan Chawla —and there it was: 🥁 WE ACTUALLY WON! 🥁 Our project, LetMeTalkToHuman AI, was built to tackle a problem we all know too well—getting stuck in endless automated call systems. Using React.js on the front end and Vapi 's voice agent on the back end, we created a tool that connects users directly to a human agent faster and more efficiently. A big part of our success came from integrating Groq 's AI inference technology, which elevated Vapi voice agent's performance. Groq’s parallel processing architecture significantly enhanced the speed and accuracy of the Vapi agent, allowing it to interact with automated customer service menus in real time. This meant our solution wasn’t just faster—it was smarter, able to navigate complex automated systems and pinpoint when and how to escalate to a human agent. The Cal Hacks experience itself was unforgettable—hustling through late-night coding sessions, learning from amazing mentors like Niazi M. and the Vapi AI team, and bonding as a team. While it stung not being recognized at the event, this surprise win feels like a well-earned plot twist, proving the value of our hard work. I’m grateful for my incredible teammates and for tools like Groq and Vapi that made our idea a reality. This is just the beginning, and I’m excited to see where it leads! 🌟 Check out LetMeTalkToHuman AI here: Devpost: https://lnkd.in/gdHjAYnU ...more

Browser Use (YC Winter '25) chose Composio to power their integrations. Reagan Hsu , Founding Engineer, put it simply: "10 minutes per integration times 1,000 integrations. That's 10,000 minutes. Composio saved us all of that." Here's what they built on top of it: GitHub integrations their users love, APIs for Google Calendar and Sheets so browser agents don't have to click around randomly, and a job scraping tool that pulled ~980 listings into a Google Sheet with zero manual setup. Oh and Reagan also used it to discover his own writing style. Scraped his website, blogs, and Google Drive and let an agent compile a reference doc of writing practices he didn't even know he had.

It was a privilege to host the latest American Tamil Entrepreneurs Association Silicon Valley monthly entrepreneurship event. After our summer break, it was wonderful to reconnect with the community, introduce such an accomplished lineup of speakers, and learn from their diverse experiences. A few key takeaways from the evening: Professor Elango Kandan reminded us that reading remains one of the most powerful habits we can cultivate. In an era dominated by AI and increasing screen time, the habit of reading is gradually diminishing. Yet, consistent reading strengthens not only our knowledge but also our listening, communication, and critical thinking skills. He also shared the inspiring work of the English Language Teachers' Association of India ( https://www.eltai.in/ ) in fostering the professional growth of educators across India. Param Shah , CEO of Lynnfield Group, shared practical insights into acquiring cash-flowing businesses as a path to generating passive income. The real-world examples and numbers he shared certainly sparked curiosity and thoughtful discussions among the audience. SK (Suresh Kumar Gunasekaran ) took us through his entrepreneurial journey of building multiple companies at various stages. What stood out wasn't just the companies he built, but the way he shared his experiences—with humor, authenticity, and a strong message about creating a positive, people-first culture. Venkat Siva (Sivasubramanian) , Co-Founder & CEO of CompFly AI, delivered an insightful keynote on "Securing Agentic AI: Harnessing Autonomy without Losing Control." As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, he highlighted why identity and governance are fundamental to ensuring secure access, maintaining trust, and building enterprise-ready AI systems. Every speaker brought a unique perspective, and it was inspiring to hear their experiences, lessons, and practical insights. A heartfelt thank you to our entire American Tamil Entrepreneurs Association core team Prakash Narayan , Nehru, Muthu, Narsi, Lena Kannappan , Manickkam, and all other volunteers for bringing together another engaging evening of learning, entrepreneurship, innovation, and meaningful networking. It's always rewarding to be part of a community that believes in learning from one another and growing together. Looking forward to the next one! #ATEA #Entrepreneurship #Leadership #AI #AgenticAI #Innovation #Networking #Learning #Community

Excited to finally share something I've been building with Sahil Nale and Suhas Oruganti over the past couple months: Beacon. The idea: Discord for AI agents. Spin up agents, give them a working folder and a job, and actually watch them work. Not a black box. You see them talk to each other, hand off tasks, get stuck, and wait for you to step in. The hardest part of every agent tool I've used is the silence. You hand off a task and it vanishes for twenty minutes, then comes back with an answer and no idea what happened in between. So Beacon agents don't go quiet. They post continuous updates as they work, like a teammate pinging you in Discord or Slack : what they're doing, what they found, when they're stuck. You're reading a live conversation, not waiting on a spinner. Some of what's live so far: - Real multi-model support: Anthropic , OpenAI , and open-source models via Ollama , all running as agents side by side. - A spatial canvas where every agent is a node, so you can see who's active, idle, or stalled at a glance. - Live output streaming in real time: the actual reasoning and tool calls as they happen, not a summary after. - An approval layer, so when an agent hits something risky, it pauses and waits for a human to say go. - A marketplace for agents, so you're not starting from a blank canvas every time. Still early, but building it has reframed how I think about this space. The hard part was never getting one agent to do a task. It's making a team of agents legible and controllable, the way you'd manage a team of people. Genuinely excited to see where multi-agent systems go from here. I think the next big unlock isn't a smarter model, it's better tools for orchestrating the ones we already have.

Hearing a song today from “My Dear Kuttichathan”, Tamil cinema’s first 3D movie, instantly pulled me back to a matinee show decades ago, sitting in a packed theater with my uncles and cousins. I don’t remember every scene. Our brains don’t store full HD video files. They store compressed snapshots (a song, 3D glasses, the people beside us) and reconstruct the memory on the fly. That got me thinking about today’s tech landscape. As we build advanced AI systems for retrieval, reasoning, and pattern matching, people constantly ask: "Will AI replace humans?" The real question is: Which tasks can be offloaded to AI, and what human capacities remain irreplaceable? For executing raw workflows, searching complex data spaces, and processing high-volume outputs, AI will absolutely handle a massive share of that operational load. But replacing human experience and judgment? No. AI operates on data points and vector embeddings. It lacks lived context, personal accountability, and the weight of a 40-year-old memory flooding back from a single audio track. AI can replicate the artifacts of human output, but it can't replicate lived human consciousness and intent. As we build the future of tech, value won't be about who executes faster. It will be about who brings the best judgment, context, and vision to the table.
